name: CapCut Turbulent Wide Angle Shake Transition
use_when: A high-energy AMV, action montage, sports edit, or social transition needs aggressive motion while staying connected to the beat.
The cut already has beat-matched clip timing and now needs a dedicated transition pass.
Wide-angle distortion, turbulence, and shake can make zooms feel more physical instead of flat.
avoid_when: The transition hides the action geography, face, caption, product, or proof.
The project tone is mature, calm, documentary, or brand-safe and aggressive shake would feel cheap.
Initial clip design is not locked enough to judge the transition flow.

timeline_pattern.pattern: locked_speed_matched_clips -> careful_splits -> turbulent_effect -> wide_angle_zoom_or_distortion -> transition_shake_pass -> impact_sfx -> readability_review
timeline_pattern.order_rule: Add transition shakes after turbulent and wide-angle effects are visible, because shake intensity depends on final transition flow.
timeline_pattern.movement_pass_rule: If a pendulum or similar movement pass is added before the transition, judge the combined swing, turbulence, wide angle, and shake together.
timeline_pattern.split_rule: Split carefully around the cut so the effect starts and resolves on intentional frames.
timeline_pattern.wide_angle_rule: Use wide-angle distortion to make zoom transitions feel more natural, but lower it if it bends the subject or captions too much.

motion.rule: Shake should peak around the cut, impact, or beat and then settle quickly enough for the next clip to read.

keyframe_values.sync_tolerance: Peak shake or impact within 1-2 frames of the cut or beat in high-energy edits.
keyframe_values.settle: Resolve the strongest shake before the next action pose needs to be read.
keyframe_values.intensity_review: Judge shake intensity only after the turbulent and wide-angle layers are applied.

sound.rule: Use a hit, whoosh, or impact only on the transition's real motion peak, and vary repeated cues.

captions.rule: Do not keep captions over the most distorted frames unless they remain readable and do not cover the action.

color.rule: Any flash, glow, or distortion tint must preserve the subject silhouette and avoid compression ugliness.

implementation.ffmpeg: Approximate with scale/crop/rotate keyframes, lens distortion where available, noise/displace overlays, and short motion blur; inspect cut frames.
implementation.remotion: Drive scale, translate, rotate, lens distortion, turbulence texture, and shake amplitude from transition frame metadata.
implementation.blender: Use camera shake, lens distortion/compositor displacement, and motion blur around the cut.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: After splitting locked clips, add turbulent effect, wide angle effect, then reapply or tune shake specifically over the transition range.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Adjustment Layers with Transform shake, Turbulent Displace, Lens Distortion or Optics Compensation, motion blur, and markers at the cut/beat.

common_mistakes: Adding transition shake before seeing how the turbulent and wide-angle effects flow.
Making the distortion so strong that the subject bends or the viewer loses the action.
Leaving captions on top of the most chaotic frames.
Using the same shake intensity on every transition.
Stacking pendulum movement, turbulence, wide angle, and shake without rechecking the next readable pose.
Adding SFX near the transition instead of on the real motion peak.
qc: Does the transition peak land within the intended beat/cut tolerance?
Is action readable immediately after the shake settles?
Do turbulent and wide-angle effects avoid bending faces, captions, products, or proof beyond recognition?
Are captions suppressed, moved, or still readable during the transition?
Does the SFX land on the actual transition peak and stay below dialogue if dialogue is present?
